evidence.conditions: Teachers can view every student interaction with MagicSchool.
evidence.quotation: Teachers can view every student interaction with MagicSchool.
evidence.notes: Explicit staff visibility into student interactions; same content is repeated in D004-B011.

evidence.conditions: Every interaction between students and MagicSchool.
evidence.quotation: Teachers can view every interaction between students and MagicSchool.
evidence.notes: Explicit access by another user, not merely tool approval.

evidence.conditions: May use, share or train systems on user data; students are directed to D20-approved enterprise tools.
evidence.quotation: Many AI apps may use, share or train their systems on user data.
evidence.notes: User data is not expressly identified as student data in the first sentence; educational context and following student direction make the connection plausible but not certain.

evidence.conditions: May use or share user data; students should use approved enterprise tools.
evidence.quotation: Many AI apps may use, share or train their systems on user data.
evidence.notes: Possible downstream handling is warned about, but the apps and data relationship are generalized.

evidence.conditions: Protocols are against unauthorized sharing of PII; compliance with laws is also specified.
evidence.quotation: protocols against unauthorized sharing of Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
evidence.notes: Explicit student-data disclosure safeguard within the Security principle.

evidence.conditions: The district disclaims responsibility for dissemination or replication of any student or staff input.
evidence.quotation: shall not be responsible for the dissemination, replication or alteration of information or data input
evidence.notes: Non-responsibility language flags downstream dissemination/replication but does not itself clearly authorize or prohibit it.

evidence.conditions: Data is shared among all users accessing the public platform, within and outside the district.
evidence.quotation: use and share data among all users who access the platform, both within and outside of the district.
evidence.notes: Definition expressly identifies disclosure to other platform users.

evidence.conditions: Right applies while using district-provided AI tools and concerns unauthorized AI training.
evidence.quotation: protect their personal data and creative works from unauthorized AI training
evidence.notes: Student right directly addresses personal data/creative works and training.

evidence.conditions: Right is to protect data and creative works from exploitation while using district-provided tools.
evidence.quotation: from unauthorized AI training or exploitation
evidence.notes: Exploitation is not specified as sale, advertising, disclosure, or another particular reuse.

evidence.conditions: Procurement and contract documents are to address contractor use of user data to train new AI systems; details are in the succeeding written-statement passage.
evidence.quotation: Use of user's data to train new Al Systems
evidence.notes: Paragraph introduces procurement language concerning data used for training; B005 is a lead-in and is not duplicated.

evidence.conditions: The model must be pre-trained and no data may be used to train a model for a new product.
evidence.quotation: no data is being used to train a model to be used in the development of a new product.
evidence.notes: Contractor statement about data use for training in procurement context.

evidence.conditions: The warning covers personal details of students and families and says information shared with GenAI could train models.
evidence.quotation: personal details of students, families, employees
evidence.notes: Training risk is explicitly connected to student/personal information; B003's input prohibitions are separate and input-only.

evidence.conditions: Prohibits tools that collect and employ user data to train or improve models; exception permits learning-model training only as curriculum instruction in a teacher-managed classroom model, not external public data/services.
evidence.quotation: Students are prohibited from using any AI tools that collect and employ user data to train or improve their underlying models.
evidence.notes: The same paragraph preserves a narrow classroom-instruction exception; do not flatten it into a simple prohibition.

evidence.conditions: District data cannot be used to train public AI models; contracts must include language noting the requirement.
evidence.quotation: District data remains District property and cannot be used by vendors to train public AI models.
evidence.notes: Explicit restriction with contractual implementation detail.

evidence.conditions: Copilot statement concerns public models and school data; MagicSchool statement says student data is never used to train AI models.
evidence.quotation: Not used to train public AI models on school data
evidence.notes: Tool-card claims are reported as district webpage content, not independently verified.

evidence.conditions: Student information entered in approved tools must stay within the BCPS environment and not train district-approved models.
evidence.quotation: student information is not used to train district-approved Artificial Intelligence models.
evidence.notes: FAQ summary distinguishes approved tools from open public tools elsewhere.

evidence.conditions: Student information entered into approved tools must remain inside the BCPS environment.
evidence.quotation: student information entered into approved tools must remain within the Broward County Public Schools environment
evidence.notes: Explicitly limits onward data flow; not merely an initial-upload rule.

evidence.actor: Approved Broward County Public Schools tools
evidence.conditions: Current district requirements prohibit using students' interactions to train AI models.
evidence.quotation: approved Broward County Public Schools tools must not use our students’ interactions to train Artificial Intelligence models.
evidence.notes: FAQ answer specifically addresses student interaction data.

evidence.conditions: Student information stays within the district environment and is shared only with authorized staff who need it; visibility varies by tool and educational or safety purpose.
evidence.quotation: is shared only with authorized staff who need it.
evidence.notes: Conditional internal disclosure and an explicit recipient/need limitation.

evidence.conditions: Current district requirements say information in approved tools stays within BCPS and cannot train models.
evidence.quotation: student information in approved tools must remain within the Broward County Public Schools environment and cannot be used to train Artificial Intelligence models.
evidence.notes: Myth-versus-fact statement; retain as a distinct paragraph-level pair.

evidence.conditions: Collection is limited to what is needed to deliver the educational service; use is for that purpose alone and not advertising or unrelated commercial use.
evidence.quotation: Information is used for that purpose alone, not for advertising or any unrelated commercial use.
evidence.notes: The sample answers section is expressly marked as draft wording to be confirmed by legal/data governance (D025-B044).

evidence.conditions: Student and staff information is not used to train public AI models; this is described as a condition of approval.
evidence.quotation: student and staff information is not used to train public AI models.
evidence.notes: Sample answer in a webpage section; distinguish district claim from verified contract terms.

evidence.conditions: Approved tools may not sell student data or use it for targeted advertising.
evidence.quotation: approved tools may not sell student data or use it for targeted advertising.
evidence.notes: Explicit vendor secondary-use restrictions.

evidence.conditions: Parent resource describes state privacy law as limiting vendor use of student data, including a ban on sale.
evidence.quotation: Limits how education vendors use student data, including a ban on selling it.
evidence.notes: Law-summary statement; not an independent vendor contract clause.

evidence.conditions: Open-source public tools may use data entered to train future models; the same text says entered data is typically stored and may be used unless stated otherwise.
evidence.quotation: data entered may be used to train future models.
evidence.notes: General explanation framed as a risk for tools used in the school context, not a claim about a named student account.

evidence.conditions: Example is Microsoft Copilot with Microsoft 365; data is not used to train models and remains within the organization environment.
evidence.quotation: Data is not used to train models and remains protected within the organization’s secure environment.
evidence.notes: Specific enterprise-system contrast to the public/open-source explanation in B013.

evidence.conditions: Explains that conversation retention is different from model training on user data.
evidence.quotation: a chatbot retaining your conversation is not the same as the GenAI model training on your data.
evidence.notes: Explanatory distinction; does not establish a vendor retention period.

evidence.conditions: Starting a new conversation or erasing memory stops the earlier memory from affecting future conversations.
evidence.quotation: if you start a new conversation window, or erase the memory, it won’t impact your future conversations either.
evidence.notes: Describes a memory-clearing action and effect, not deletion from provider backups or training corpora.

evidence.conditions: If Google saves a conversation and uses it to determine response patterns for anyone in the future, that is described as training on user data.
evidence.quotation: If Google saves your conversation and uses it to determine patterns that inform how the model responds to anyone in the future
evidence.notes: Explicit example of downstream training; student use is not specified in the example itself.

evidence.conditions: User/stakeholder information could train models unless the company has an approved district data privacy agreement; the paragraph warns of possible public-domain access.
evidence.quotation: any information provided—whether through prompts entered by the user or AI-generated responses—could potentially be used by companies to train their models unless that company has an approved data privacy agreement with the District.
evidence.notes: Risk statement and agreement exception; not an absolute prohibition.

evidence.conditions: Information could become accessible in the public domain unless explicitly told otherwise.
evidence.quotation: could become accessible in the public domain unless explicitly told otherwise.
evidence.notes: Possible disclosure is expressly warned about, but no specific sharing practice or vendor is identified.

evidence.conditions: Staff may enter confidential data only into tools with approved data privacy agreements; staff are advised to turn off chat history and data training settings.
evidence.quotation: staff are advised to turn off chat history and data training in the settings
evidence.notes: Advice to disable data training is not a claim that the setting deletes data already processed.

evidence.conditions: Staff are advised to turn off chat history; the text does not specify retention duration or deletion from provider stores.
evidence.quotation: turn off chat history
evidence.notes: Setting may limit future history but does not clearly establish a deletion procedure or retention window.

evidence.actor: Foundational model vendors and application layer vendors
evidence.conditions: Stakeholder information and CPS intellectual property may not be used for training/fine-tuning or shared with foundational model vendors without explicit permission.
evidence.quotation: Foundational model vendors must ensure that stakeholder information, copyrighted material, or proprietary CPS intellectual property is not used to train their models without explicit permission.
evidence.notes: Application-layer vendor's separate fine-tuning/sharing rule appears in the same paragraph.

evidence.conditions: Sharing stakeholder information with the foundational model vendor is barred absent explicit permission.
evidence.quotation: shared with the foundational model vendor without explicit permission.
evidence.notes: Explicit third-party disclosure condition.

evidence.conditions: Vendors must document how their tool collects, stores, uses, and protects data as a factor in approval.
evidence.quotation: Vendors must provide comprehensive documentation regarding their tool’s data privacy practices, including how data is collected, stored, used, and protected.
evidence.notes: Vendor-practice documentation is a review requirement; the excerpt does not specify a particular use or sharing rule.

evidence.conditions: Enterprise data-share agreements say models will not be trained on interaction data.
evidence.quotation: agreeing not to train their models on or store any data from interactions with their product
evidence.notes: Training and storage are both stated; separate retention evidence is recorded for the same paragraph.

evidence.conditions: Enterprise agreement says interaction data will not be stored; no timeframe/exception is specified.
evidence.quotation: not to train their models on or store any data from interactions with their product
evidence.notes: Storage is addressed as a retention prohibition, not merely geography/security.

evidence.actor: SchoolAI and its contracted large language model providers
evidence.conditions: Contracted agreements ensure personal student data is not saved or used by third parties to train/refine future models.
evidence.quotation: ensure personal student data is not saved or used by third-parties to train or refine future models.
evidence.notes: Vendor claim on district resource webpage; not independently verified.

evidence.actor: SchoolAI and its contracted large language model providers
evidence.conditions: Personal student data is stated not to be saved.
evidence.quotation: personal student data is not saved
evidence.notes: Explicit no-save claim; no retention period is given.

evidence.conditions: The tool does not sell student data and prohibits behavioral tracking.
evidence.quotation: SchoolAI does not sell student data and prohibits behavioral tracking.
evidence.notes: Explicit sale and behavioral-tracking restrictions.

evidence.conditions: No use of district data for training new products without prior written DCS approval and documented scope.
evidence.quotation: There shall be no use of district data for training new products without prior written DCS approval and documented scope.
evidence.notes: Same paragraph bars vendor access absent a signed data-processing/security agreement and requires adherence to deletion schedules.

evidence.conditions: No vendor may access district data without an executed DCS Data Processing & Security Agreement.
evidence.quotation: No AI vendor may access district data without an executed DCS Data Processing & Security Agreement
evidence.notes: Access condition concerns vendor access to district data, not merely users entering prompts.

evidence.conditions: Vendor must adhere to district data minimization and deletion schedules.
evidence.quotation: adherence to district data minimization and deletion schedules.
evidence.notes: Explicit deletion-schedule requirement.

evidence.conditions: Pretrained model; no data is used to train a model for a new product.
evidence.quotation: no data is being used to train a model to be used in the development of a new product
evidence.notes: Contractor statement requested in procurement.

evidence.conditions: Restriction applies to data in raw, aggregated, processed, or transformed form and to a new Contractor product/model/service/offering.
evidence.quotation: expressly prohibited from using any data provided to it by the data providers—either in its raw form or after undergoing any form of processing, aggregation, or transformation—for the purpose of training a new AI System
evidence.notes: Appendix A sample contractual clause, not verified executed contract language.

evidence.conditions: Customization or development for district-specific needs is allowed only with prior written DCS approval and under applicable law and contract terms.
evidence.quotation: Any such use of the data for the district-specific needs shall be subject to prior written approval by the Dothan City School District
evidence.notes: Explicit exception to the general new-product training prohibition in B024; preserve conditional nature.

evidence.conditions: Written data-use explanation must state duration of data usage; this is a request for information rather than a fixed duration.
evidence.quotation: Duration of data usage.
evidence.notes: Procurement request documents duration but does not set a maximum retention period.

evidence.conditions: Training data must be deleted or returned by a certain date; lawful/contractual retention requires segregation/protection and a deletion certificate by agreed date.
evidence.quotation: Deletion of training data or training data will be returned by a certain date.
evidence.notes: Appendix sample completion statement includes a defined-date deletion/return process and retention exception.

evidence.conditions: Information entered into GenAI may be accessible to others due to data sharing or breaches; users are told to exercise caution and not enter sensitive/confidential data.
evidence.quotation: Information entered into GenAI may be accessible to others due to data sharing or breaches.
evidence.notes: Risk warning links user information to possible disclosure, but does not identify the actual recipients or a sharing rule.

evidence.conditions: Sample family questions ask whether a tool collects, shares, or stores personal information and what it does with data.
evidence.quotation: Does the tool collect, share, or store personal information?
evidence.notes: Questions for evaluation, not a statement of a vendor's practice.

evidence.conditions: Asks whether data can be deleted later or removed after a change of mind.
evidence.quotation: Can data be deleted later?
evidence.notes: Vetting question only; no deletion right or process is established.

evidence.conditions: Families are advised to discuss what information a tool collects and how it may be used.
evidence.quotation: Discuss what kind of information the tool collects, how it may be used, and whether data can be deleted.
evidence.notes: Family guidance prompts review but does not establish a downstream use rule.

evidence.conditions: Families are advised to ask whether data can be deleted.
evidence.quotation: whether data can be deleted.
evidence.notes: Question/advice does not establish a deletion right or timeline.

evidence.conditions: Inappropriate disclosure of student data is named as a risk of AI use.
evidence.quotation: inappropriate disclosure of student data
evidence.notes: Risk statement in guiding principles; distinct from the following input restriction in B005.

evidence.conditions: Unauthorized disclosure of protected student/employee information is prohibited; selected information may be sent in encrypted form with Superintendent/designee permission.
evidence.quotation: shall not use technology resources for unauthorized disclosure of personal or student information
evidence.notes: Narrow, permission-based exception for encrypted sending is in the same paragraph.

evidence.conditions: Evaluation must protect against unlawful disclosure of student information.
evidence.quotation: protecting from unlawful disclosure of student information
evidence.notes: Explicit protection tied to student information; not inferred from FERPA citation alone.

evidence.conditions: Tools within Houston ISD domain do not use chat history to train models; HISD has data-sharing agreements with named providers.
evidence.quotation: chat history is not used to train the models.
evidence.notes: Enterprise account distinction is explicit; public consumer tools are treated separately.

evidence.conditions: Sensitive data shared with the enterprise tool is not shared back with AI for training.
evidence.quotation: any sensitive data that is shared with this tool does not get shared back with the AI for training purposes.
evidence.notes: Explicit data-flow limitation in tool rationale.

evidence.conditions: Information entered outside district-managed platforms may be shared with the company operating the tool.
evidence.quotation: any information entered may be shared with the company that operates the tool.
evidence.notes: Conditional risk warning; no named consumer service's actual terms are established.

evidence.conditions: These tools do not use student or staff data to train external models.
evidence.quotation: These tools do not use student or staff data to train external AI models
evidence.notes: FAQ distinguishes district-managed environment from consumer services.

evidence.conditions: Student PII disclosure is subject to Education Law 2-d and applicable third-party agreements; staff must consult the Data Protection Officer.
evidence.quotation: particularly whenever student Personally Identifiable Information is disclosed, including third-party agreements where applicable.
evidence.notes: Paragraph establishes compliance/consultation requirements around disclosure, without stating a blanket ban.

evidence.conditions: Input may be used for training or redistributed unless the provider explicitly confirms compliance and guarantees no reuse for future model training; teacher/staff tool choice remains contextual.
evidence.quotation: guarantees that input information will not be reused for future AI model training
evidence.notes: Conditional vendor assurance; the paragraph explicitly recognizes tool/task differences.

evidence.conditions: Provider must explicitly confirm compliance and no reuse for future training before sensitive material is entered; redistribution to others is identified as a risk.
evidence.quotation: may potentially be stored, accessed, or redistributed by the system.
evidence.notes: The same paragraph warns of onward availability and requires assurances; not an unqualified prohibition.

evidence.conditions: Information input into unapproved tools may be used for algorithm training; users are prohibited from entering specified protected information.
evidence.quotation: may be used for algorithm training and made available to other users of the system outside the district.
evidence.notes: Warning describes both training and disclosure; the separate prohibition is input-only.

evidence.conditions: Input may be made available to other users outside the district.
evidence.quotation: made available to other users of the system outside the district.
evidence.notes: Explicit potential disclosure to other platform users.

evidence.conditions: Data-sharing agreements between vendors and school systems must be crafted to comply with privacy regulations and safeguard sensitive student information, including recordings.
evidence.quotation: Data-Sharing Agreements (DSAs) between AI vendors and school systems must be crafted to ensure compliance with privacy regulations and safeguard sensitive student information
evidence.notes: General DSA requirement; the excerpt does not enumerate permitted uses, redisclosure limits, or retention terms.

evidence.conditions: Enterprise accounts should ensure prompts and responses are not used to train foundation models.
evidence.quotation: ensure that data protection includes safeguards to ensure that prompts and responses are not used to train foundation models.
evidence.notes: Explicitly tied to prompts/responses and school accounts.

evidence.conditions: Rubric asks whether identifiable student/employee/user data is excluded from training, product improvement, analytics, or future model development unless authorized through school-system legal/privacy process.
evidence.quotation: not used for model training, product improvement, analytics, or future AI model development unless expressly authorized
evidence.notes: Evaluation question, not a confirmed vendor restriction; authorization exception is explicit.

evidence.conditions: Rubric asks about opting out of model training or secondary data use and what data may be collected/used.
evidence.quotation: Can the school system opt out of model training or secondary data use?
evidence.notes: Vetting question, not a statement that opt-out is available.

evidence.conditions: Rubric asks how long data is retained, when deleted, and whether termination/non-renewal triggers return and certified deletion within a defined period, including backups.
evidence.quotation: Does the vendor provide clear policies for how long data is retained and when it will be deleted?
evidence.notes: Evaluation question and checklist, not a confirmed vendor term.

evidence.conditions: Upon termination or non-renewal, rubric asks for usable data return and certified deletion within a defined period, including backups.
evidence.quotation: Upon termination or non-renewal, does the vendor return all school-system data in a usable format and certify deletion within a defined period
evidence.notes: Termination/non-renewal is expressly connected to data return/deletion, so it qualifies.

evidence.conditions: Privacy risks include limited transparency about how vendors store, use, or share data.
evidence.quotation: limited transparency about how vendors store, use, or share data.
evidence.notes: Risk statement, with no specific data flow or student-data practice identified in this paragraph.

evidence.conditions: Families must be told what data is collected, how long retained, and when opt-out applies.
evidence.quotation: how long data are retained
evidence.notes: Explicit retention-duration transparency requirement.

evidence.conditions: Unrelated model training is prohibited; vendors must meet education-focused practice standards.
evidence.quotation: prohibit advertising, profiling, or unrelated model training
evidence.notes: Same paragraph also sets secondary-use and data-retention/deletion limits; separate category rows follow.

evidence.conditions: Contracts must limit data use, prohibit advertising/profiling, require disclosure of data practices, and comply with breach-notification laws.
evidence.quotation: contractual limits on data use, retention, and deletion; prohibit advertising, profiling, or unrelated model training
evidence.notes: Disclosure subcode reflects required disclosure of vendor data practices, not breach notification alone.

evidence.conditions: Contracts must set limits on retention and deletion; vendor use is barred if it cannot demonstrate secure education-focused practices.
evidence.quotation: contractual limits on data use, retention, and deletion
evidence.notes: Explicit retention and deletion provisions.

evidence.conditions: Contracts must limit data use and sharing; documentation must disclose collection, retention, model-training practice, and other vendor data practices.
evidence.quotation: Contracts must include data minimization, limits on data use and sharing
evidence.notes: The requirement is embedded in procurement/vendor governance guidance.

evidence.conditions: Vendors must document data use for training; tools lacking transparency are not adopted.
evidence.quotation: Vendors must provide clear documentation on AI techniques, data collection and retention, use of data for model training
evidence.notes: Disclosure/documentation requirement; no blanket no-training rule in this paragraph.

evidence.conditions: Contracts must contain clear termination and data-deletion provisions and limit retention.
evidence.quotation: clear termination and data deletion provisions.
evidence.notes: Termination is directly tied to deletion here.

evidence.conditions: Vendor questionnaire may ask how long systems retain data and the process for secure deletion.
evidence.quotation: Data retention and deletion policies: how long the system retains data, and the processes for securely deleting it.
evidence.notes: Procurement question/checklist rather than an established limit.

evidence.conditions: Possible implementation success metric is zero advertising/secondary uses.
evidence.quotation: Zero advertising/secondary uses
evidence.notes: Metric recommendation; not an existing vendor prohibition.

evidence.conditions: AI must protect student education records and meet parental consent requirements.
evidence.quotation: AI systems must protect the privacy of student education records and comply with any parental consent requirements.
evidence.notes: Summary of legal-facing protection; not inferred from the legal citation alone.

evidence.conditions: Data must remain under MPS direct control.
evidence.quotation: Data must remain within the direct control of MPS.
evidence.notes: Explicit control limitation on data flow.

evidence.conditions: Teacher evaluation asks how data is collected and used and whether practices meet standards.
evidence.quotation: How is data collected and used, and does it meet data practices standard?
evidence.notes: Question for review, not a described use or restriction.

evidence.conditions: LEAs should not allow their data to be used to train vendor models; this can be negotiated with vendors.
evidence.quotation: LEAs should not allow their data or information to be used to train the vendor’s models.
evidence.notes: Student data concerns are explicit earlier in the same paragraph; advice to negotiate is not a confirmed contract term.

evidence.conditions: Best practice says to ensure data retention alongside privacy compliance and security, without a duration or deletion step.
evidence.quotation: ensure data privacy compliance, data retention, and robust security measures
evidence.notes: Retention is mentioned but the kind of retention safeguard is unspecified.

evidence.conditions: Tool table says name, school account, and prompts are collected and shared only as necessary under the Google Workspace for Education agreement.
evidence.quotation: Shared only as necessary under Google Workspace for Education agreement
evidence.notes: The table is a district summary of the Gemini entry.

evidence.conditions: Tool table says student ID, progress data, and assessment results are shared under district agreement.
evidence.quotation: Shared under district agreement
evidence.notes: The table identifies student-level information and a district agreement.

evidence.conditions: Student guidance asks whether a system is selling user data and what it does with user data; students are told to understand the privacy policy before sharing personal information.
evidence.quotation: is the system “selling” your data to other parties, etc.
evidence.notes: Question and literacy discussion, not evidence of an actual sale.

evidence.conditions: Students are asked to think critically about how systems are trained and what they do with user data.
evidence.quotation: how AI systems are trained, what the systems do with user data
